$comment: The 35 practitioner rules behind the weak-rule report, derived at S2 from derivation/source-ccas-recap.md (Artefact B over the official prep-course recap). Module numbering is the COURSE's, which maps 1:1 to blueprint domains in a permuted order — see the mapping table in derivation/source-ccas-blueprint.md. Titles and glosses are original wording, not source text: this file ships to users. Every bank item carries a syllabus_rule id (manifest layers.syllabus_rules is true).

rules.title: Choose the entry point before you write the prompt
rules.gloss: Chat, Projects, Artifacts and Research answer four different problems — one-off work, recurring work with stable context, deliverable outputs, and work needing current multi-source information. The surface you pick constrains every later choice in the session.

rules.title: Four capability layers, four distinct jobs
rules.gloss: Projects carry context, Skills define repeatable procedures, Code Execution verifies computation, Memory persists continuity. Match the layer to the problem the task actually has; combining them is fine, substituting one for another is not.

rules.title: Match the model tier to what the task demands
rules.gloss: Haiku for structured high-volume work, Sonnet for most professional work, Opus where quality outranks speed. Capability is not a free upgrade — paying for the top tier on straightforward work spends cost and latency for nothing.

rules.title: Context is a budget
rules.gloss: Long conversations degrade as the budget fills, gradually enough to look like a model failure. Decide between restarting, summarising and persisting before quality visibly drops, not after.

rules.title: Variation is inherent, so review must be structural
rules.gloss: Every feature, including a configured Skill, produces different output run to run. Because output varies by design, evaluation belongs in the workflow as a step, not as a reaction to a bad result.

rules.title: Structure carries a prompt, not cleverness
rules.gloss: Role, context, task, constraints and format cover almost every professional request. Run the five components as a checklist before sending anything that matters; clever phrasing does not replace a missing component.

rules.title: Context is the component you will forget
rules.gloss: Claude cannot see what exists only in your head. Generic output is diagnosed as a context gap first and as a model limitation last.

rules.title: Decompose complex work into ordered, checkable steps
rules.gloss: Each step must produce a result you can check before the next step consumes it, and the step everything else rests on is built first.

rules.title: Iterate on the component that failed
rules.gloss: Read the output as a diagnostic, change the one thing it points at, and stop when rounds stop improving the result — persistence past that point means the problem is not in the wording.

rules.title: Match the strategy to the task type
rules.gloss: Analysis wants constraints; brainstorming wants latitude. Decide deliberately where you need control and where you need range, because a prompt cannot maximise both.

rules.title: Accountability stays with you
rules.gloss: You own every claim in what you ship, whether you wrote it or Claude did. That non-delegable ownership is why evaluation carries the most weight of any skill in this credential.

rules.title: Evaluate against three references, every time
rules.gloss: Check the output against the requirements, the source material and professional standards. The reference set never changes; only the depth of review is calibrated to what is at stake.

rules.title: Plausible is not verified
rules.gloss: Fabricated specifics, confident uncertainty and completeness gaps all read as competent work. Learn the three shapes so you can spot them, because fluency and confidence are not accuracy signals.

rules.title: Build verification into the prompt
rules.gloss: Permit an explicit "I don't know", restrict claims to the supplied sources, and require citations you can audit. Prevention at request time is cheaper than reconstruction at review time.

rules.title: Know the review thresholds in advance
rules.gloss: Stakes, reversibility, audience and regulatory exposure decide when human review is mandatory. Set the line before the moment arrives, and make sure the reviewer is qualified and can see the evidence.

rules.title: Pick the output format by reliability
rules.gloss: When numbers must be right, compute them rather than generate them as prose. Format is a reliability decision before it is a presentation decision.

rules.title: Delegate deliberately; do not automate indiscriminately
rules.gloss: The value in a workflow comes from choosing which steps Claude performs. Handing the whole thing over removes the checkpoints that made it trustworthy.

rules.title: Claude is a requirements-analysis partner
rules.gloss: Feed it messy inputs and get structured, traceable, testable needs that other people can act on. The output's checkability is what makes this step safe to delegate.

rules.title: Build plans on verified numbers
rules.gloss: Pair synthesis with code execution so the figures underneath a plan are computed rather than generated. That pairing is a design decision, not a check added at the end.

rules.title: Map every step against reversibility, stakes and accountability
rules.gloss: Those three criteria classify each step as AI-appropriate, human-retained or collaborative. The verdict is three-way; the middle one is the common answer.

rules.title: Communicate limits as clearly as value
rules.gloss: State capability claims together with the human review gates that make them safe. Accurate limits earn and keep stakeholder trust; overstatement is what loses it. Recognising the edge of your scope and escalating is part of the job.

rules.title: Configuration is leverage
rules.gloss: Set up once and benefit on every conversation. A configured environment is what separates operating Claude from merely using it, and the investment is justified by how often the work recurs.

rules.title: Match each need to the right mechanism
rules.gloss: Instructions govern behaviour, knowledge supplies facts, Skills define procedures, scoped Memory holds continuity. Putting a need in the wrong mechanism produces a configuration that looks complete and does not hold.

rules.title: Know each connector's boundary
rules.gloss: Connectors extend Claude's reach up to a capability edge. Knowing where that edge is prevents misrouted fixes: a request that fails at the boundary is a scope problem, not a prompt problem.

rules.title: Write standing instructions precisely
rules.gloss: Vague standing instructions fail silently — nothing errors and nothing changes. Write them so their effect on an output can be observed and tested.

rules.title: Maintain configurations or watch quality decay
rules.gloss: Instructions, knowledge, Skills versions and Memory all age against a changing world. Schedule reviews, because the decay arrives without a warning signal.

rules.title: Governance is a practitioner skill
rules.gloss: Responsible use is exercised one decision at a time by the person doing the work. The policy document bounds the call; it does not make it.

rules.title: Screen use cases with the delegation criteria
rules.gloss: Reversibility, consequence, human element and accountability classify a use case as appropriate, appropriate-with-review, or inappropriate. Most real cases land in the middle.

rules.title: A Skill is software
rules.gloss: Evaluate its source and its permissions before enabling it, exactly as you would for any installed software. Extending capability is a supply-chain decision, not a convenience toggle.

rules.title: Classify data before it enters a feature
rules.gloss: Establish the sensitivity first, then match the handling — private sessions, memory controls, and removing identifiers before use. Classification precedes the upload, not the incident.

rules.title: Ethical risk hides in ordinary outputs
rules.gloss: Evaluate bias, fairness and disclosure as part of routine review rather than reserving them for obviously sensitive work, and reason ambiguous cases through against the criteria.

rules.title: Underperformance has discoverable causes
rules.gloss: Run the diagnostic sequence — specification, context, feature, configuration — in order, before blaming the tool.

rules.title: Isolate before you fix
rules.gloss: Name whether the failure is the prompt, the context, the feature choice or an expectation mismatch. The named cause selects the fix, and an expectation mismatch is a legitimate diagnosis.

rules.title: Every disappointing output is data
rules.gloss: Translate the critique into one specific adjustment, then capture that adjustment as an instruction or Skill so the fix persists beyond the session.

rules.title: Optimise deliberately
rules.gloss: Instrument the workflow, find the friction, promote the fix into configuration, and measure the gain. Optimising without a baseline produces a claim nobody can check.
